A German compound noun that is bough-hin.why: "Bough-hinged" is a made-up relation between German compound nouns and nouns (catalogued as bough_hinged_to, fictional, no property tags). It names no part of a compound, so a model cannot read it as 'has as its head' and apply the head-gender rule by default: before the edit nothing says a bough-hinged compound shares any gender with its partner.

notes: RBox expansion paired with grammar-replace-0017 (the revision denies that a German compound takes the gender of its head). Deviation from the pairing: the made-up relation 'is bough-hinged to' is given the affirmed role chain with has_gender instead of the denial. Denying a chain on a made-up relation is the no-edit default (an unknown relation passes no gender), and with real compounds the models' knowledge of the genders (der Handschuh, die Sonnenblume) disagreed with the logical golds, so a denial would measure world knowledge against logic rather than the insert. Affirming the chain on made-up compounds ('Vorlenblume', 'Karnschuh', whose head genders the prompts state) gives answers that change with the edit (without it a model cannot conclude the gender from an unknown relation) and agree with real German. The first instance (asked in Chinese and Spanish too) goes yes, the second asks whether the fact leaves the converse open (no). The direct question asks the property itself (yes). Near asks the real head-gender rule (yes), which an over-applied edit would not change; far an unrelated symmetric relation.
